sections.title: Welcome
sections.purpose: What iCLEANED does and what you will be asked.

sections.title: Scenarios
sections.purpose: A scenario is one complete description of a livestock enterprise for one year. Open one, copy one, or start a new one.

sections.title: Your livestock system
sections.purpose: A few questions about what you keep and how, so we only ask what applies to you.

sections.title: Place, climate, seasons and land
sections.purpose: Where the animals are, what the year looks like there, and the land that feeds them.

sections.title: What the model counts
sections.purpose: Background: where the enterprise starts and stops, and what stays outside it.

sections.title: Land & {plot}s
sections.purpose: Describe each {plot} that grows feed or is grazed. Feeds are linked to {plot}s later.

sections.title: Seasons
sections.purpose: The feeding periods of the year.

sections.title: Herds
sections.purpose: Group animals that are kept together and managed the same way.

sections.title: Animals
sections.purpose: Describe each group of animals separately, because they eat and produce differently.

sections.title: Feeds
sections.purpose: List every feed the animals eat during the year, where it comes from and how it is grown.

sections.title: Fertiliser products
sections.purpose: The nitrogen content of each fertiliser you use. How much you spread, and where, is on the feed cards.

sections.title: Manure & inputs bought in
sections.purpose: Manure, compost or bedding brought in from outside adds nitrogen to the land.

sections.title: Feeding plan
sections.purpose: For each animal group, what share of what they eat in this season comes from each feed?

sections.title: Losses after the {gate}
sections.purpose: Optional: milk and meat lost between the producer and the consumer.

sections.title: Check & run
sections.purpose: Fix anything blocking, review what we assumed, then run.

sections.title: Results
sections.purpose: Results will appear here after running.

sections.title: Parameter set
sections.purpose: The reference values this scenario starts from. Shipped sets are read-only; make your own copy to change values.

sections.title: Batch processing
sections.purpose: Check, compile and summarise many enterprises at once from a spreadsheet or a JSON file.

sections.title: Help, FAQ and contact
sections.purpose: Common questions, what to do when you are stuck, and how to reach the team.

systemQuestions.label: What does this scenario describe?
systemQuestions.help: CLEANED is a livestock enterprise model: a herd, the land that feeds it and its manure. The same description works from one household to a national herd; only the numbers change.

options.label: One enterprise (a household or a farm)
options.definition: One herd, the land that feeds it and its manure. Crops that are not fed to the animals stay outside.

options.label: A group of enterprises (village, cooperative, project)
options.definition: Enter totals, or one typical enterprise and how many it represents.

options.label: A district or region
options.definition: Enter the herd and land totals for the area; defaults come from the area's climate and soils.

options.label: A national herd
options.definition: Totals for the country; one row per animal category.

systemQuestions.label: What is the main purpose of the cattle?
Do you grow any of the feed yourselves?
systemQuestions.help: Grass, fodder crops, crop residues from your own fields.

systemQuestions.label: Do you buy or collect any feed from outside the {enterprise}?
systemQuestions.help: Bought concentrate or hay, or grass cut from roadsides and communal land.

systemQuestions.label: Do you bring manure, compost or bedding in from outside the {enterprise}?
Do you use mineral fertiliser on feed plots?
How many feeding seasons does the year have?

options.label: One: feeding is the same all year
Two: for example rainy and dry

systemQuestions.label: Is any of the feed grown as paddy rice?
Are there trees in the feed plots?

herdPatterns.label: Always in a shed or pen (zero-grazing)
Shed at night, grazing {onfarm} by day

manureOptions.label: Left where it drops in the field or pasture
manureOptions.definition: Nothing is collected; dung stays on the land.

manureOptions.label: Spread on fields within a day
manureOptions.definition: Collected and applied fresh, no storage.

manureOptions.label: Piled or heaped in the open
manureOptions.definition: Stored as a solid heap for weeks to months.

followups.label: Is the heap covered or compacted?
Is straw, sawdust or stover mixed in?

manureOptions.label: Left to build up in an open pen or dry lot
manureOptions.definition: Dung accumulates on the pen floor and is cleared occasionally.

manureOptions.label: Left to build up as bedding inside the shed
manureOptions.definition: Deep litter; dung and bedding build up and are removed later.
manureOptions.ipcc: Cattle and swine deep bedding > 1 month

followups.label: Is it cleared more than once a month?
followups.yes: Cattle and swine deep bedding < 1 month

manureOptions.label: Stored wet in a pit, tank or slurry pond
manureOptions.definition: Liquid or slurry storage below or beside the animals.

followups.label: How long is it usually stored?

manureOptions.label: Composted deliberately
manureOptions.definition: Turned or aerated on purpose to make compost.

options.label: Static pile with pipes or a fan
In a drum or closed vessel

manureOptions.label: Fed to a biogas digester
manureOptions.definition: Typical fixed-dome digester with covered storage.
manureOptions.ipcc: Anaer digester, Low leak, HQ stor, LQ tec

manureOptions.label: Dried and burnt as fuel
manureOptions.definition: Dung cakes or dried manure used as household fuel.

fields.label: Scenario name
fields.help: Something you will recognise later, for example "Njombe baseline 2026" or "Njombe + Napier".

fields.label: What are you testing?

options.label: Baseline: the enterprise as it is now
options.definition: Describe what happens today. Every comparison needs one.

options.label: Intervention: a change to test
options.definition: A copy of a baseline with one or more things changed, for example a new feed or covered manure storage.

options.label: Training or example
options.definition: For learning or demonstration; not a real enterprise.

fields.definition: A baseline describes the enterprise as it is now. An intervention is a copy with something changed, so the two can be compared.

fields.label: Defaults from
fields.definition: The parameter set that supplies reference values (animal weights, feed quality, soils). Recommended from the location.

fields.label: {location}
fields.help: Click the map or choose country, region and district.

fields.label: How many enterprises does this scenario represent?
fields.definition: Enter the herd and land as totals across the group, or as one typical enterprise and give the number it stands for.

fields.label: World region
fields.definition: Region used for IPCC livestock defaults; set from the country.

fields.label: Climate type
fields.definition: IPCC climate class. It sets manure methane and soil carbon factors.

options.label: Tropical, wet
options.definition: Hot all year; rain most months (over ~2000 mm).

options.label: Tropical, moist
options.definition: Hot all year; rainy and dry seasons (~1000–2000 mm).

options.label: Tropical, dry
options.definition: Hot all year; long dry season (under ~1000 mm).

options.label: Tropical highlands
options.definition: Tropics above ~1000 m; cooler nights.

options.label: Warm temperate, moist
options.definition: Mild winters, warm summers; rain exceeds evaporation.

options.label: Warm temperate, dry
options.definition: Mild winters, warm summers; evaporation exceeds rain.

options.label: Cool temperate, moist
options.definition: Cold winters; rain exceeds evaporation.

options.label: Cool temperate, dry
options.definition: Cold winters; evaporation exceeds rain.

options.label: Boreal, moist
options.definition: Long cold winters; moist.

options.label: Boreal, dry
options.definition: Long cold winters; dry.

fields.label: Rainfall in a normal year
fields.definition: Total rain the {farm} receives in an average year.
fields.help: For example 1100 for the Njombe highlands.

fields.label: Months with rain in a normal year
fields.definition: Calendar months in which meaningful rain usually falls.
fields.help: Tap the months. Two rainy seasons are fine.

fields.label: Evaporation demand (ET0)
fields.definition: Water that would evaporate from well-watered grass. A climate property, not something you measure.

fields.label: Main soil type
fields.definition: Soil group of the feed plots (FAO/WRB). Plots can override this.

options.label: Nitosol
options.definition: Deep red clay soil, common in highlands.

options.label: Cambisol
options.definition: Young, moderately developed soil.

options.label: Lixisol
options.definition: Strongly weathered, low nutrient reserve.

options.label: Acrisol
options.definition: Acid, clay-rich subsoil; low fertility.

options.label: Andosol
options.definition: Dark volcanic soil; fertile, erodes easily.

options.label: Fluvisol
options.definition: River-deposited soil in valleys and floodplains.

options.label: Vertisol
options.definition: Heavy black clay that cracks when dry.

options.label: Phaeozem
options.definition: Dark, humus-rich soil of grasslands.

options.label: Xerosol
options.definition: Dry-region soil, little organic matter.

fields.label: Soil organic carbon
fields.definition: Carbon in the top 30 cm of soil.

fields.label: Soil total nitrogen
fields.definition: Total N in the topsoil. If you only have %, multiply by 10.

fields.label: Soil depth
fields.definition: Depth of soil counted for carbon stock (IPCC default 0.3 m).

fields.label: Area
fields.help: 1 acre ≈ 0.4 ha. Used to weight soil and practice when plots differ.

options.label: Flat
options.definition: You can walk it easily; water hardly runs off.

options.label: Hilly
options.definition: Noticeable slope; you lean walking up.

options.label: Steep
options.definition: Hard to plough with oxen.

options.label: Very steep
options.definition: Terraces needed to farm.

fields.label: Length of the slope
fields.definition: Distance water runs from the top of the {plot} to the bottom or to a terrace.

fields.label: What covers the ground most of the year?
fields.definition: Sets how well the soil is protected from rain.

fields.label: Soil on this {plot}
fields.definition: Only if it differs from the {farm}'s main soil.

fields.label: How much organic matter goes back to the {plot}?

options.label: High, without manure: residues and cover crops

Herd name

fields.label: Where do these animals spend their time?
fields.definition: Sets a starting time budget for each group in the herd; you can adjust per group.

fields.label: Of the manure you collect from this herd, how much stays {onfarm}?
fields.definition: The rest is sold or given away.

fields.label: Animal group
fields.definition: Category from the parameter set; sets the default weight and milk composition.

fields.label: Your name for this group
fields.help: Optional, e.g. 'Improved dairy cows' or 'Mama Neema's heifers'. The model still uses the standard category; your name is kept alongside it.

fields.label: {numbers}

fields.help: Average number present during the year. At regional or national scale, the population in this category.

fields.label: Average live weight now

fields.label: Weight when fully grown
fields.definition: Mature weight this animal will reach; used for growth energy.

fields.label: Milk per cow per day
fields.definition: Average over the milking period, including milk fed to calves.
fields.help: For example 4 in the morning and 2 in the evening = 6.

fields.label: Weight gained per animal per year
fields.definition: Live-weight gain over 12 months.
fields.help: A calf going from 90 to 150 kg in a year gains 60.

fields.label: How much of the main product is fed to the animals?

Cattle - Cows (local).label: Cows, local breed
Cattle - Cows (local).definition: Mature cows of indigenous or unimproved breeds; typically 300–400 kg, low to moderate milk.

Cattle - Cows (improved).label: Cows, crossbred or improved
Cattle - Cows (improved).definition: Mature cows with exotic blood (Friesian, Ayrshire crosses); typically 380–600 kg.

Cattle - Cows (high productive).label: Cows, high-producing
Cattle - Cows (high productive).definition: Intensive dairy cows giving over ~8,500 kg milk a year.

Cattle - Calves.label: Calves (under 1 year), local
Cattle - Calves.definition: Young stock of local breeds still growing.

Cattle - Steers/heifers.label: Heifers and steers (1–3 years), local
Cattle - Steers/heifers.definition: Growing animals not yet calved or finished.
